comment: The contract cases of the Rust core and of the bindings generated from it (binding design K-1, G-5), one group per member of packages/rust/interface.json; packages/rust/tests/contract_cases.rs runs each case against the core. The keys of a case are the parameter names of its member. An instance is {"new": <member that gives it>, "receiver", "args", "then": [steps]}; a callback is {"callback": {"<callback member>": [rows]}} and a function {"function": [rows]}, a row being {"args", "result"} with "once" for a row that answers one call, and a call that no row answers fails the case. A template_value and a json_value are {"kind", "value"}, a map being its [key, value] pairs in order and a number of a json_value its literal; a map<T> of the contract, such as define, is an object of its entries in order; {"host": "object"} is a native object; a source is its text or {"hex"}; a variant is {"type": "<case value>", fields}, a record an object of its fields, an enum the value of its variant and bytes {"hex"} (CNF-19); a path is relative to the directory of the case. A failure is raises: its kind, its status and its category (ERR-1, B-4); a result is the returned value, and a returned instance is observed by a case of its own member, whose receiver the call makes; a case names no after. A case that names faults arms those fault injection points before its call (G-5, X-1): a kind of the category internal, which no input reaches, has the case of its point and no input case. The group template_value holds the cases of the value alias, {id, value, raises}: value_in refuses the value with the kind, one of the in_raises of the alias (binding design U-7).
